# The midpoint and radius of an interval, two-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_mid_rad_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The midpoint $m$ and the radius $r$ of the interval $[x_l, x_u]$, with the values of `mid` and `rad` of IEEE 1788 for an unbounded or empty interval:

$$[m - r, m + r] \supseteq [x_l, x_u].$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x_l = x_{l0} + x_{l1}$, $x_u = x_{u0} + x_{u1}$, $m = m_0 + m_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.midpoint()` | `Interval<T, 2>` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | $m$; computes the whole kernel, as the other does: `X.mid_rad()` gives both from one call; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |
| `X.radius()` | `Interval<T, 2>` | `T` | $r$; computes the whole kernel, as the other does: `X.mid_rad()` gives both from one call; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |
| `X.mid_rad()` | `Interval<T, 2>` | `MidRad<T, 2>` | $m$ and $r$ from one call; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $[x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- If $[x_l, x_u]$ is bounded: $m$ is finite, $x_l \le m \le x_u$, $\lvert m - \tfrac{x_l + x_u}{2}\rvert \le \frac{3u^{2}}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert \tfrac{x_l + x_u}{2}\rvert + 2\eta$, and $[m - r, m + r] \supseteq [x_l, x_u]$. The radius $r$ may be $+\infty$ for a bounded interval near the top of the range (an infinite radius contains everything); it is finite when $\lvert x_l\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max}-2}$ and $\lvert x_u\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max}-2}$.
- The whole line gives $m = 0$, $r = +\infty$; $[x_l, +\infty]$ with $x_l$ finite gives $m = \Omega$, the largest finite number of `T`, and $[-\infty, x_u]$ gives $m = -\Omega$, both with $r = +\infty$; the empty set gives a NaN in every limb. These are the values of `mid` and `rad` of IEEE 1788.
- In every case the midpoint $m$ is a canonical number of two limbs: two NaN for the empty set, two zeros for the whole line, $(\pm\Omega, +0)$ for a half-line, and a normalized pair for a bounded interval.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_mid_rad_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_mid_rad_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_mid_rad_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the sum of the halves of two limbs, moved into the interval, and the larger bound of the distance to a bound (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_mid_rad_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_mid_rad_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_pow2_2`](mul_pow2_2.md), [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md), [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md), [`add_ball_2_2`](add_ball_2_2.md), [`to_up_2`](to_up_2.md), [`radd`](radd.md).

```
# The midpoint and a radius of an interval with 2-limb bounds (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", "Midpoint, radius and the conversions"): the steps of interval_mid_rad_1 on kernels of
# two limbs. The bounds brought into [-Omega, Omega] (the half-lines, by their leading limbs); the
# halves by mul_pow2_2, exact but for a limb that is an odd multiple of eta, and one limb of a
# normalized pair at most is, so that each half is within eta/2 of its value; their sum by add_2_2,
# within 3u^2/(1-4u) of the sum of the halves; the move into [l, h] by lt_2_2 (it brings the midpoint
# closer); each side of the radius by radd(to_up_2(z), e), (z, e) = add_ball_2_2 of the difference,
# at least the difference, and the larger side. So for a bounded interval: l <= m <= h, m normalized,
# |m - (l + h)/2| <= 3u^2/(1-4u) |(l + h)/2| + 2 eta, and [m - r, m + r] contains the interval; the
# smallest radius is not claimed. Near the top of the range a side of the radius is not finite (radd
# steps past Omega, or a TwoSum of add_2_2 overflows inside and gives a NaN): it is made +inf, a radius
# with which every ball contains the interval; the radius is finite when both bounds are at most
# 2^(emax-2) in magnitude, where add_2_2 stays finite. As for one limb: the whole
# line has midpoint 0, a half-line the largest finite number of its sign, both with radius +inf (the
# values of IEEE 1788); the empty set gives three NaN. In every case the midpoint is a canonical
# 2-limb number, the invariant of the k-number midpoint() returns: two NaN, two zeros, (+-Omega, +0),
# or a normalized pair (ball_of_interval with ieee1788 and a center of two limbs claims it).

om             = pred(const inf)
mo             = neg(om)
ml             = lt(xl0, mo)
l0             = select(ml, mo, xl0)
l1             = select(ml, 0, xl1)
mu             = lt(om, xu0)
h0             = select(mu, om, xu0)
h1             = select(mu, 0, xu1)
(hl0, hl1)     = mul_pow2_2(l0, l1, const up(1/2))
(hu0, hu1)     = mul_pow2_2(h0, h1, const up(1/2))
(ma0, ma1)     = add_2_2(hl0, hl1, hu0, hu1)
ca             = lt_2_2(ma0, ma1, l0, l1)
mb0            = select(ca, l0, ma0)
mb1            = select(ca, l1, ma1)
cb             = lt_2_2(h0, h1, mb0, mb1)
mc0            = select(cb, h0, mb0)
mc1            = select(cb, h1, mb1)
nl0            = neg(l0)
nl1            = neg(l1)
(za0, za1, ea) = add_ball_2_2(mc0, mc1, nl0, nl1)
ta             = to_up_2(za0, za1)
rs             = radd(ta, ea)
fa             = lt(rs, const inf)
ra             = select(fa, rs, const inf)
nm0            = neg(mc0)
nm1            = neg(mc1)
(zb0, zb1, eb) = add_ball_2_2(h0, h1, nm0, nm1)
tb             = to_up_2(zb0, zb1)
rt             = radd(tb, eb)
fb             = lt(rt, const inf)
rb             = select(fb, rt, const inf)
rm             = lt(ra, rb)
rc             = select(rm, rb, ra)
md0            = select(ml, mo, mc0)
md1            = select(ml, 0, mc1)
me0            = select(mu, om, md0)
me1            = select(mu, 0, md1)
bo             = and(ml, mu)
mf0            = select(bo, 0, me0)
mf1            = select(bo, 0, me1)
un             = or(ml, mu)
rd             = select(un, const inf, rc)
ne             = lt(xl0, const inf)
m0             = select(ne, mf0, const nan)
m1             = select(ne, mf1, const nan)
r              = select(ne, rd, const nan)
```

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
